concerns.text: Task T001 is tagged `[P1]` indicating it is parallel‑safe, but it produces artifacts (requirements.txt, download script, checksum file) that are required by subsequent tasks (T002‑T005). The task has implicit ordering dependencies and therefore is not safe to run in parallel.

Task T002 is tagged `[P1]` yet depends on the raw data produced by T001 and on the successful execution of the download script. This creates a hidden ordering requirement, violating the parallel‑safe contract.
Task T003 is marked `[P1]` but builds a FAISS index that consumes the parquet file created by T002. The task cannot be safely executed in parallel with its producer.
Task T004 carries `[P1]` while it loads the FAISS index generated by T003. Its correct operation depends on the prior completion of T003, so it is not parallel‑safe.

Task T005 is labeled `[P1]` yet runs an end‑to‑end benchmark that requires the baseline and semantic‑decay retrievers (from T003 and T004) and the validation set created by T005 itself. It cannot be executed in parallel with its producers.

Task T006 is tagged `[P2]` (parallel‑safe) but performs a deterministic grid‑search that reads the validation set produced by T005 and the memory‑node parquet from T002. It must run after those producers.
Task T007 carries `[P2]` yet depends on the optimal parameters from T006, the FAISS index from T003, and the processed memory nodes from T002. It cannot be parallel‑safe.
Task T008 is marked `[P2]` but consumes the evaluation queries generated by T007. It therefore has an ordering dependency.
Task T009 is labeled `[P2]` while it assembles a report from artifacts produced by T006, T007, and T008. It must run after those tasks.

Task T010 is tagged `[P2]` but its unit tests validate code produced in earlier tasks (T003, T004). Although tests could run after code is written, the tag suggests they are safe to run in parallel with code generation, which is inaccurate.
Task T011 carries `[P3]` yet references many artifacts generated throughout the pipeline (e.g., evaluation_report.json, figures). It must be executed after all those producers.
Task T012 is marked `[P3]` but generates visualisations that depend on the evaluation report and figures produced by earlier tasks. It cannot be parallel‑safe.
Task T013 is labeled `[P3]` yet orchestrates the entire pipeline, invoking scripts that must run in a specific order. The `[P]` tag incorrectly suggests it can be run in parallel with other tasks.
Task T014 carries `[P3]` but aggregates and documents artifacts from the whole pipeline, requiring that all prior tasks have completed. It is not parallel‑safe.
